title: Governance Readiness Judge
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: AI-Native Schools
description: Judge six fictional districts as not ready, ready for Level 3, or well placed for Level 4 by applying the must-have and should-have rule.

learningObjectives: The learner will judge whether each of six districts is not ready, ready for Level 3, or ready for Level 3 and well placed for Level 4, by applying the must-have and should-have rule, correctly judging at least five of six on the first attempt.
prerequisites: Governance readiness, the six must-have and four should-have practices, and the readiness rule, from the section "Governance Readiness" in Chapter 10

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Commit an answer, get feedback with the reason, and review what was missed
commonMisconceptions: Many should-have practices can make up for a missing must-have
A district with one strong feature is ready
Readiness is a score out of ten
assessmentOpportunities: A district has every practice except M6, a breach response plan. What is the verdict?
A district has all six must-haves and two should-haves. What is the verdict?
Is readiness a score out of ten?

controls.name: Choice buttons
controls.description: commit an answer. A wrong first answer gives a hint and lets you choose again; only the first answer counts.

controls.name: Show definitions
controls.description: opens or closes the reference table. Reading it is exploration, not evidence.

controls.name: Next
controls.description: moves to the next item after feedback. On the results screen, Previous missed and Next missed step through what you missed.

controls.name: Play again
controls.description: starts a practice run with the items reshuffled. Practice runs do not change the first-run score.
